name: Grand piano v2 (Yamaha C5)

source.author: Alexander Holm
source.format: 48 kHz / 24-bit FLAC, stereo AB pair of AKG C414
source.licence_quote: Creative Commons Legal Code / Attribution 3.0 Unported (the repository's LICENSE file); README: 'Author: Alexander Holm'
source.credit: Piano: Salamander Grand Piano V3 by Alexander Holm, CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Retuned, trimmed and re-encoded for this app.
source.changes_made: retuned per note, 48 kHz to 44.1 kHz, onset trim, tail trim with fade, peak normalisation, MP3 encode

format.note: ffmpeg/Chrome/Firefox trim the 1105-sample MP3 delay from the LAME tag. Decode _click.mp3 once in the app and subtract where the click lands, so a decoder that ignores the tag stays aligned.

note_spacing: minor third (the source is sampled in minor thirds; playback shifts +-1 semitone)

articulations.release_hammer: key-up hammer/damper noise, 30 notes, mono, play at key release (source sfz volume -37 dB, veltrack 82 %)
articulations.release_resonance: string resonance after key-up ('harmL'), 23 notes, play at key release for velocity 45+ (source sfz volume -4 dB, rt_decay 6-9 dB/s)

tail_note: layers 2, 4 and 6 use 0.8x these lengths; the last 30 % of every file is a cosine fade to zero

tuning.method: fundamental measured per file (zero-padded FFT, parabolic peak); one correction per note = target minus the median of its 8 layers; a take more than 2 cents from that median gets its own correction (files[].cents_applied)
tuning.target: equal temperament from A2 up; below A2 a bass stretch of 0.5 cent per semitone (-12 cents at A0)
tuning.why_not_the_published_table: Data/tune_ret.txt matches the measured fundamentals only above C6. From A1 to C3 it leaves the fundamentals 10 to 22 cents flat, so the corrections here are measured, and the published values are kept below for reference.

gain.meaning: apply at playback to the peak-normalised file. It restores the piano's own dynamics, smoothed across notes inside each layer. 0 dB is the loudest file.
